_comment: KNOWN-GAP REPRODUCTION (C) for layout/erc/adc_block.supply-spec.json's
`devices[]` block. Not an item-11 artifact -- never cite this run as
evidence about this block.
Byte-identical to the supply spec except that `devices[]` is removed
entirely, i.e. the pre-klayout-tools#2183 behaviour: every drawn device
body on a declared role is read as a wire.
EXPECTED OUTCOME: `gates[]` contains a net whose label set is
`XCMP.pon,XCMP.pop,vdd` -- the comparator's two preamp output nodes
fused to the `vdd` rail through the two poly load-resistor bodies,
which this graph cannot tell from poly wire. `vdd` still resolves to
exactly one island, so the supply verdict itself does not flip here;
what the carve-out buys is that the island is the RAIL and not the
rail-plus-two-signal-nodes, and that the two resistor bodies stop
contributing non-physical antenna area to it.
WHY THIS IS COMMITTED: the supply spec justifies its `devices[]` block
by naming this fusion. That justification is only worth anything if
the fusion is reproducible, so it is re-run and asserted by
`run_erc.py` rather than asserted in prose. The mirror-image risk --
a `devices[]` marker that over-covers real routing and CUTS it -- is
guarded from the other side, by the supply case's own zero-finding
expectation and by the `body_area_um2` values it pins.
